narratives.Overview:
## What happened

Later labs (5, 7, 9, 10, capstone) dispatch CLI verbs with:

```js
if (process.argv[1] && resolve(process.argv[1]) === fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)) {
  console.log(main());
}
```

`path.resolve` does not realpath. On macOS `/var` is a symlink to `/private/var`. If the helper is invoked via a `/var/folders/...` path, `argv[1]` and `import.meta.url` differ, `main()` never runs, Node exits 0, and stdout is empty.

`lab_root="$(node "$helper" create)"` then becomes empty. Subsequent `git -C "$lab_root"` and `node "$lab_root/node_modules/.bin/directive"` run against the wrong tree (or `/node_modules/...`).

## Repro

```sh
# helper via /var path (no-op, exit 0, no stdout)
node /var/folders/.../lifecycle-lab.mjs create

# helper via realpath (prints the repo root)
node /private/var/folders/.../lifecycle-lab.mjs create
```

Observed 2026-09-12 on macOS with the course extracted under `$TMPDIR`.

A checkout under `$HOME` that is not reached through `/var` will not hit this. A learner who copies the course to `/tmp`, or whose `pwd` is not `-P`, can.

Lab 7 instructions use `course_root="$(pwd -P)"`, which usually saves a careful learner. Lab 2 and ad-hoc helper paths do not always.

## Suggested repair

Compare `realpathSync(process.argv[1])` to `fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)`, or always `import.meta.url` as the CLI entry without argv identity checks. Fail loudly if the entry did not run (`create` must not exit 0 with empty stdout).

clauses.text: Invoking each affected lab helper through the macOS /var alias runs its CLI entry instead of exiting successfully with empty output.
Lab 2 does not overwrite a learner-supplied curriculum root and uses isolated public-registry npm configuration for the normal path while retaining an explicit provided E401 exercise.
Lab 9 fallback invocation and capstone blank-title assertions accept implementations that follow the surrounding fixture contract.

Learner-facing material uses a capability-based Node requirement, warns about command-specific --help side effects early, labels the known doctor false negative, and keeps authoring-runtime drift out of the learner baseline summary.
